excerpts.text: 5 July 1907: LSQ leaves NY for Seattle; 19 July 1907: arrives Dawson; spends three days there (PI summary)

“there persons concerned in the reported mammoth find would make no reasonable agreement as to showing the body and feeling pretty well satisfied that there was nothing in their various stories” (as quoted in the Tale; the PI timeline gives ‘The persons concerned …’)
“sailed to Keewalik at the eastern end of Kotzebue Sound,” … “a few miles up Keewalik River,” … “to ‘the spit.’”

“a clumsy, waterlogged canoe…finally secured only by chance.” … “for cook and helper” … “fishing boat hired for the coasting; Keewalik’s three launches were under contract and could not be procured at any price.” … “made it impossible to sail in any wind ahead of the beam and caused a considerable loss of time.”
“Several unavoidable delays”

“portions of a mammoth skeleton together with some skin and hair…embedded…in such a manner as to afford very good reasons for the belief that the entire skeleton, with a large part of the covering, would be found in place” (Tale)
“considerable ice around the edge of the Bay, the bluff had begun to freeze, and even the exposed clay flat was solid” (PI timeline, 19 September 1907)
“owing to the inevitable delays in Alaskan travel” (2 November 1907); “very hard labor” (Tale fn 45)
“toward the end of May” 1908: LSQ leaves NY (PI); “after ten days’ delay in the ice” (21 June 1908)
20 July 1908 Buckland; 20 August 1908 back to Keewalik; 23 September 1908 New York (PI summary)
“with picks”; “unfortunately”; “crowded together in an area about ten by seven feet”; “no doubt” … land slide (Tale)
“a small, thin sheet of chewed grass cut out of the frozen sandy silt close to the lower jaw,…as brilliantly green as on the day it grew” (Tale)
“a sudden fall of temperature cannot be called upon, as has been frequently done, to account for the extinction of Pleistocene mammals and the preservation of their flesh” (Tale)

“commonly used term ‘ice-cliff,’” … “obviously erroneous” … “fossils have never been found imbedded in pure-ice-masses and the term is particularly misleading since it implies that preservation of flesh and hair is due to the ice” (Tale, with LSQ's footnote to Adams in the Journal du Nord)
